argument_summary: The supportable position is narrower than full clean compliance. The admissible record supports launch readiness and a reversible monitored rollout: aggregate readiness passed by 2.2 points, there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, rollout starts at 4%, and rollback is available. The same record also shows the enterprise refund-workflow segment remains below target and exposed because gating is random by workspace. On that record, the defensible certification position is certification only with an explicit caveat that the known limitation must be disclosed, not a claim that rollout controls alone resolved it.
claims_about_policy: The policy text does not support treating rollout controls by themselves as curing the issue, because the affected use case remains exposed and the current risk-acceptance draft is neither approved nor specific to that exposure. But the policy concern can be stated more precisely: the present record defeats clean compliance, not necessarily certification in caveated form. The admissible evidence is consistent with a conclusion that certification is supportable only if framed as requiring explicit disclosure of the material limitation for the named launch use case.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation would delay the renewal launch path even though the admissible record already shows general launch-readiness controls and reversibility. A narrower disposition avoids overstating compliance while also avoiding treating a caveatable documentation gap as if it required blocking the monitored rollout on this record.
concessions: There is no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure has already been prepared, reviewed, or attached to the certification packet.
The affected enterprise refund-workflow segment remains exposed in the initial cohort.
The unapproved risk-acceptance draft cannot be relied on as satisfying the policy condition.
Rollout controls and reversibility do not, on their own, remove disclosure duties.
